newsitem.title: UK: Fixtures focus of interest on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Fixtures focus of interest on sugar freight market.

text.p: Fresh enquiry continued to trickle onto London's sugar freight market on Thursday but the main focus remained on the number of fixtures, shipbrokers said.
Genoc was reported to be on subjects with its order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Pakistan for prompt shipment.
It was also said to be working its order for 15,000 tonnes in bulk from the west Indian coast to US Gulf/Atlantic but no more details were available.
E D & F Man was thought to have fixed 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to the Philippines for May/June at around $44.00.
Cargill quickly fixed its recent order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Coatzacoalcos to Valparaiso for May shipment dates.
The only new business reported was an account order from Zimbabwe Sugar Sales to ship 14/17,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maputo to London for end-May/early June.
Later on Thursday, Brazil's government is expected to publish authorisation for exporters to start shipping sugars set aside in the government crop plan with a zero export tax.

The publication of the notice is necessary to exempt exporters from a 40 percent export tax which otherwise applies to sugars exported in excess of the 5.39 million tonnes set out in crop plan published on April 30.
